title: Rulebook Relay
user: Daily-puzzle regulars bored of word clones who want one mobile-friendly browser puzzle with a fresh but learnable rule twist each day.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN poster explicitly asks whether there is a daily puzzle where the rules change every day and whether there would be interest.
A federated repost of Gerrymandle describes a daily puzzle where players redraw electoral districts, showing appetite for a daily format with a non-word core mechanic.

recurrence: The explicit 'rules change every day' request is reinforced by a current daily game built around a distinctive systemic mechanic rather than another word grid.
current_workaround: Maintain a bookmark folder of many daily games, accept repeating mechanics, or play one-off puzzle archives.
incumbents_and_gap: Wordle, Connections, Puzzmo, and numerous -dles deliver routine, while daily experimental games can be opaque. There is room for a predictable learning scaffold around rotating rules.
smallest_useful_product: A one-screen daily logistics puzzle: slide three couriers across a 6×6 board in under 40 moves while one printed 'rule card' changes (mirrors, shared fuel, one-way bridges, etc.). A 30-second interactive example teaches that day's mutation; a six-day week ends with a remix. Inputs are tap/drag or arrows; each attempt is 3–8 minutes. Non-goals: word lists, AI-generated riddles, streak penalties, and social posting gates.
success_measure: At least 40% of day-one players return for three distinct rule cards in the first week, while tutorial abandonment remains under 20%.
monetization: free — a daily link should have zero first-run friction; a one-time archive/supporter unlock may follow only if it does not fragment the daily puzzle.
constraints: Every daily seed must be solvable and independently verified; avoid real election content or political targeting despite the cited genre example; cache puzzles and store streaks locally by default.
why_distinct: The product is a carefully authored rule-language and teaching pattern, not an automated stream of generic daily puzzles.
